chapter: The McShann band on the road and at the Savoy
title: Ramey's scrapbook and John Tumino's sacrifices
summary: Ramey gave his scrapbook and telegram to Tumino and never got them back; Tumino went without for the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But the thing is, now, when you go East, we haven't talked about that, when you go East with McShann to play at the Savoy Ballroom, opposite Lucky Millinder, what happened there?

Well, we had gotten a telegram and McShann doesn't even remember this. But Johnny Tunno brought us a telegram and I had that in my scrapbook for a long time, and I gave it to Johnny after we got to New York, and I never got it back. And the same way with those pictures that you have of the pre-McShann band? I was the only one that kept a scrapbook. I had everything that happened.
Who did you give them to?
Johnny Tunno, who was the boss of the band.
And I never got it back. But --
He was in New York then, was he?
No, he was still travelling with us.

And, man, he really sacrificed for this band. A lot of time he and his family would go hungry, Bird or somebody of them would come and get his last dollar or something, or come get money from his wife.
And he's so anxious to keep the band happy and everything. His wife and all of them would --
